proposal: The Mandate recommends that DOL use its oversight of the Federal Retirement Thrift Investment Board to prohibit Thrift Savings Plan investment in China, and that Congress enact a statutory bar. It also recommends that DOL remove mutual fund window options that encourage ESG and clarify the plan's fiduciary duties, that the government move management away from two named asset managers, that DOL consider enforcement actions against them, and that Congress give the board authority and guidelines for proxy voting.

status_summary: S. 1368, the TSP Fiduciary Security Act of 2025, was introduced in the Senate on 2025-04-09 and referred to the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee. It would bar mutual fund window funds from holding securities of China-based entities, add a national security fiduciary duty, and direct DOL regulations presuming that investments in listed Chinese military companies or Entity List firms breach it. H.R. 7357, the TSP Fiduciary Security Act of 2026, was introduced on 2026-02-04 and referred to the Oversight and Government Reform Committee, per the GovInfo bill status record. No executive order or DOL or board action on China exposure after 2025-01-20 was found.

timeline.event: S. 1368, the TSP Fiduciary Security Act of 2025 (Senator Rick Scott), was introduced in the Senate, read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs; the bill status record lists no later action.

H.R. 7357, the TSP Fiduciary Security Act of 2026 (Representative Randy Fine), was introduced in the House and referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform; the bill status record lists no later action.

title: Bar Thrift Savings Plan investment in China and remove ESG-oriented fund options
